slots.meaning: The small group of young investigators, named as a group at the opening.
slots.guidance: A plural group of two to four peers, read as a sentence subject ('{HEROES} find ...'); capable together, no adult leader among them.

slots.meaning: The locked civic landmark the whole story takes place inside.
slots.guidance: One old, publicly known building with a working mechanism at the top, read after 'find'; imposing but never sinister, and plausibly enterable by children.

slots.meaning: The community the landmark belongs to, restored by the triumphant ending.
slots.guidance: The surrounding town or neighbourhood, read after 'lost to' and 'bring it to'; a place with a shared history worth recovering.

slots.meaning: The kind of puzzle the whole mystery is built on.
slots.guidance: A bare singular noun for a decodable system, used adjectivally too ('the {CIPHER} note', 'a second tiny {CIPHER} panel'); solvable by a determined child with the right tool.

slots.meaning: The gruff, kindly adult custodian who can let the friends in and knows the history.
slots.guidance: One adult caretaker of the landmark, read as a sentence subject and after 'with'; brusque but safe, and the one who catches the thieving ending without any menace.

slots.meaning: The long-dead craftsperson who built the landmark and hid the secret in it.
slots.guidance: One historical maker, read in the possessive ('{MAKER}'s study', '{MAKER}'s secret'); absent from the present action, known only through their work and letter.

slots.meaning: The great mechanism at the top, where the puzzle is finally set.
slots.guidance: The landmark's large public-facing mechanism, read after 'up to' and 'behind'; must have adjustable parts a solved code can be entered into.

slots.meaning: The hidden chamber the solved puzzle opens, holding the maker's legacy.
slots.guidance: One small concealed room, read after 'reveal' and 'into'; a reward space, never a trap.

slots.meaning: The landmark's working device, running true again in the best ending.
slots.guidance: A bare singular noun read after 'the' in 'the {MECHANISM} runs true again'; the thing the community would notice being fixed.

slots.meaning: The maker's trade, seen half-finished in the hidden workshop.
slots.guidance: A bare mass noun for the maker's kind of work ('clockwork', 'joinery'), read after 'half-finished'; something a child could find wondrous.

slots.meaning: The high, awkward opening that is the second unofficial way in.
slots.guidance: An opening well above ground level, read after 'through' and 'up to'; a small thrill to use, and safely landable on the far side.

slots.meaning: The low opening the decoded note points to as a way in.
slots.guidance: A ground-level gap the note can mention by name, read after 'and' and 'Try'; unglamorous and easy once known about.

slots.meaning: The physical opener the decoded clue leads the friends to.
slots.guidance: One small findable object that opens the front door, read after 'find' and 'with'; hidden in plain sight rather than guarded.

slots.meaning: The maker's own workroom inside the landmark, holding the decoding tool.
slots.guidance: One preserved private room belonging to MAKER, read as a sentence subject and after 'Open'; cluttered with the maker's papers.

slots.meaning: The absorbing stack of records that can swallow a whole evening.
slots.guidance: A plural noun for readable historical records, read after 'old', 'the fascinating', and 'Lost in the'; tempting rather than useful, since losing the night to them is one ending.

slots.meaning: The device found in the study that explains how the code works.
slots.guidance: One portable object that decodes CIPHER, read after 'holds' and 'Take'; carried up to the mechanism, so hand-sized.

slots.meaning: The one genuinely risky interior space, crossable with care or refusable.
slots.guidance: An interior space with a moving part and a narrow way past, read after 'past', 'along', and 'away from'; mild peril only, and backing out must always read as sensible rather than cowardly.

slots.meaning: The tool won past the hazard, which later frees the jammed mechanism.
slots.guidance: One portable maintenance item, read after 'grab' and 'with'; its only job is to undo the jam, which is what makes crossing the hazard worth it.

slots.meaning: The small keepsake hidden in the stair, pocketable in passing.
slots.guidance: One tiny object of the maker's trade, read after 'hides'; a collectible with no mechanical use, so finding it never gates anything.

slots.meaning: The working guts of the landmark, filling the basement.
slots.guidance: A mass or plural noun for the mechanism's inner workings, read after 'holds'; impressive to look at, not a puzzle to solve.

slots.meaning: The alternative discovery behind the mechanism: the maker's private workroom.
slots.guidance: One concealed room belonging to MAKER, read as a sentence subject and after 'into'; a wonder rather than a prize, since its ending is warm rather than triumphant.

slots.meaning: The wondrous object in the vault, beside the letter and the treasure.
slots.guidance: One charming made object of the maker's craft, read in a list after a comma; delightful and harmless.

slots.meaning: The signal that the night is over and the friends must leave.
slots.guidance: A plural or mass noun that can 'ring', read as a sentence subject; a deadline the landmark itself announces, with no one scolding them.

slots.meaning: Ending title: they lost the night to the records and left empty-handed.
slots.guidance: A title-cased phrase naming the absorbed-in-reading ending; rueful and affectionate, never a rebuke.

slots.meaning: Ending title: they found the maker's hidden workroom instead of the vault.
slots.guidance: A title-cased phrase naming the hidden-room discovery; warm and satisfying, a different prize rather than a lesser one.

slots.meaning: Ending title: the main triumph, the decoded message given back to the town.
slots.guidance: A title-cased phrase naming the full solve; quietly triumphant, and the one that reads as the story's true ending.
